title: HB1120 (2023 Regular): "Mississippi School Safety Guardian Act"; create to allow governing bodies of schools to designate employees to carry concealed firearms.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Mississippi) (gun-policy Stage 5, Mississippi); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Mississippi text (Introduced; official copy, https://billstatus.ls.state.ms.us/documents/2023/html/HB/1100-1199/HB1120IN.htm)
provenance.note: As-filed text (introduced); no date in text. No vote recorded. Guardian training, funding and identity secrecy are part of the gun-carry programme, so treated as one subject. Section 2 (Miss. Code § 45-1-2) also tells the Public Safety commissioner to set guidelines for active-shooter response (not quoted). Section 3 also lets guardians carry in schools, colleges and school athletic events (quoted only for elementary and secondary school facilities).

operative_text:
Section 1 (new, Miss. Code § 45-9-181): (3) (a) The governing body of a school, in consultation with school administrators and the Mississippi Department of Public Safety, may designate employees to participate in a School Safety Guardian Program developed by the Department of Public Safety, by which designated and trained school employees are authorized to carry concealed firearms for the protection of the students, employees and others on the campus of the school. (b) The scope and purpose of a School Safety Guardian Program includes responding to an active shooter situation or other situation that would cause death or bodily harm on the school campus or in the immediate vicinity of the school campus. The guardian's weapon shall always remain under his or her physical control while such person remains on the school campus.
Section 1 (new, Miss. Code § 45-9-181): (4) A designated school safety guardian is immune from civil liability for any action taken by the guardian if the action in question occurs during the reasonable exercise of and within the course and scope of the designated guardian's official duties. School safety guardians are charged with these duties and must act in accordance with these duties to maintain their certification and immunity. If a school safety guardian is found to have failed to carry out their official duties the immunity described in this subsection shall be waived.
Section 1 (new, Miss. Code § 45-9-181): (5) School safety guardians shall be paid a monthly stipend of Five Hundred Dollars ($500.00) by the school district.
Section 1 (new, Miss. Code § 45-9-181): (7) To be eligible for the immunity provided in this section: (a) The School Safety Guardian Program must, at a minimum, require each designated member of the program who is not a law enforcement officer, as defined in Section 45-6-3, to: (i) Possess a firearms license issued under Section 45-9-101 and complete an instructional course in the safe handling and use of firearms as described in Section 97-37-7;
Section 3 (Miss. Code § 45-9-101): Any elementary or secondary school facility, except as provided in Section 45-9-181;
Section 4 (Miss. Code § 97-3-15): (j) When necessarily committed in the performance of duty as a member of a School Safety Guardian Program as described in Section 45-9-181.
Section 5 (Miss. Code § 97-37-9): (k) That at the time he or she was a member of a School Safety Guardian Program, and was then actually engaged in the performance of his or her duties as such and met the requirements of Section 45-9-181.
